transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi… um, I’m here because I’ve been having this problem after I eat too much. I end up going to the bathroom and making myself throw up because I’m scared I’ll gain weight. And it’s not just like it happened once or twice and I felt bad about it — it’s gotten to where I keep doing it, and I’m honestly scared I can’t stop. It’s embarrassing to say out loud, but that’s why I came in.

Can you tell me more about these times when you feel like you’ve eaten too much — do you ever feel like you’re eating a very large amount of food in a short time, more than most people would eat in similar circumstances?

Yeah… yes. That’s exactly what happens. It’s not like just having an extra serving at dinner. It’s usually later at night, after the house is quiet and nobody’s really around or paying attention. I’ll go into the kitchen and it kind of starts with, like, “I’ll just have a little of the leftovers,” or a bowl of cereal or something, but then it keeps going.

I’ll eat leftovers straight from the fridge, then cereal, then chips, then ice cream if it’s there… just whatever is around and easy to grab. And it’s fast, too, not like sitting down to enjoy a meal. I’ll be standing there in the kitchen, opening cabinets and the fridge over and over, and before I really stop myself, half the pantry looks like it’s been picked over. It’s way, way more than what I think most people would eat at one time. It feels past a normal meal.

During these times when you're eating this large amount of food, do you feel like you can't stop yourself or control what you're doing, like it's happening automatically and you're just going through the motions?

Yeah… that’s probably the worst part of it, honestly. It doesn’t feel like I’m choosing each thing. Once I start on those nights, it’s like my hands just keep grabbing food, opening things, taking bites, going back for more, even while in my head I’m saying, “Lucy, stop it. Knock it off. What are you doing?”

But I don’t feel like I can actually make myself stop in that moment. It’s almost like I’m watching myself do it, like I’m on autopilot. I keep thinking, “Okay, this is the last thing,” and then I’m right back in the cabinet or the fridge again. I don’t really feel back in charge until it’s already over, when I’m looking at what I ate and realizing how far it went. Then I feel awful, but during it… no, I don’t feel in control.
How has this behavior been affecting your life — have you noticed it causing you distress or interfering with things like work, relationships, or daily activities?

Yeah… it’s definitely affecting things. More than I wanted to admit, I think.

I’ve started skipping things I used to actually enjoy, like church potlucks. I’ll tell people I’m busy or that I’m not feeling great, but really it’s because there’s all this food out, and everyone’s watching what everybody brought, and I get so tense thinking about what might happen afterward. Same with some family dinners. I don’t want to sit there worrying the whole time about whether I’m eating too much, or if I’m going to go home and… do what I’ve been doing.

And my husband notices. He can tell I’m not just relaxing and enjoying being around people. I’ll be sitting there at the table, trying to act normal, but I’m kind of stiff and quiet, and I’m thinking about the food instead of the conversation. He’ll ask me later, “Are you okay? You seemed nervous,” and I just feel awful because it’s supposed to be time with family or church friends, not this whole battle in my head. So yes, it’s causing me a lot of distress, and it’s starting to make me avoid people and things I normally care about.
How often do you find yourself making yourself vomit after these episodes of overeating — is this something that happens at least once a week, or more frequently?

Yeah… it’s at least once a week. Honestly, for the past three months or so, I don’t think there’s really been a week where it didn’t happen.

It’s usually after one of those late-night episodes, when I’ve eaten way too much and I’m just standing there feeling sick and panicked and ashamed. Then I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. Some weeks it’s not just once, either. It can happen several times in a week, especially if I’m home more because my back is acting up and I’m not as busy or distracted.

I hate saying that out loud, but… yes. It’s been happening pretty regularly.
